reading.title: The Evolution of Mercantilism and Its Economic Impact
reading.passage:
Mercantilism, an economic theory that dominated European thought from the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries, fundamentally shaped the development of global trade and colonial expansion. Proponents of mercantilism believed that a nation's wealth was directly proportional to its accumulation of precious metals, particularly gold and silver. This ideology prompted governments to implement protectionist policies, including high tariffs and trade restrictions, to maximize exports while minimizing imports. Consequently, nations competed fiercely to establish monopolies over trade routes and colonial territories, leading to intense geopolitical rivalries.

The mercantilist system, though economically flawed by modern standards, catalyzed significant institutional and technological innovations. Governments invested heavily in naval development and infrastructure to facilitate commerce, inadvertently advancing maritime technology and establishing banking systems. However, the excessive focus on bullion accumulation created artificial scarcity and distorted international trade patterns. By the late eighteenth century, economists such as Adam Smith critiqued mercantilism's fundamental assumptions, arguing that wealth derived from productive capacity and specialization rather than metal hoarding. This intellectual shift precipitated the transition toward free-market capitalism and laissez-faire economics.

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 중상주의; 국가의 부를 귀금속 축적으로 측정하는 경제 이론
보호주의적인; 국내 산업을 외국 경쟁으로부터 보호하는
독점권; 특정 상품이나 서비스에 대한 배타적 통제권
촉발했다; 무언가를 일어나게 하는 원인이 되다
자유방임주의; 정부가 경제에 최소한으로 개입하는 경제 체제

questions.q: According to the passage, what did mercantilist economists believe determined a nation's wealth?
options: Its productive capacity and specialization
The accumulation of precious metals like gold and silver
The establishment of free-market capitalism
Its investment in banking systems
questions.explanation: 두 번째 단락에서 '중상주의자들은 국가의 부가 귀금속, 특히 금과 은의 축적에 정확히 비례한다고 믿었다'고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the long-term effects of mercantilism?
options: It successfully prevented all international trade conflicts
It led to technological advances but ultimately was replaced by competing economic theories
It remains the dominant economic system in modern Europe
It had no significant impact on institutional development
questions.explanation: 지문은 중상주의가 기술 혁신을 촉발했지만, 결국 아담 스미스 같은 경제학자들의 비판으로 자유 시장 자본주의로의 전환을 초래했다고 설명합니다.

questions.q: The word 'catalyzed' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: Prevented
Triggered or brought about
Analyzed
Rejected
questions.explanation: 'Catalyzed'는 '촉발했다' 또는 '일어나게 했다'는 의미이며, 이 문맥에서 중상주의가 기술 혁신을 '야기했다'는 뜻입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention Adam Smith in the passage?
options: To show that he invented mercantilism
To demonstrate that he supported protectionist policies
To illustrate how economic thinkers challenged mercantilist assumptions and contributed to the shift toward free-market economics
To explain why mercantilism was the most effective economic system
questions.explanation: 아담 스미스는 중상주의의 기본 가정을 비판하고 부의 원천을 다시 정의함으로써 자유 시장 경제로의 전환을 이끈 인물로 제시됩니다.

sentences.original: Mercantilism, an economic theory that dominated European thought from the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries, fundamentally shaped the development of global trade and colonial expansion.
sentences.paraphrase: From the sixteenth through eighteenth centuries, mercantilism—a prevailing economic ideology in Europe—exerted profound influence over how global commerce and overseas territories developed.
sentences.tip: 명사구를 전치사구로 변환하고 동사 'shaped'를 'exerted influence over'로 대체하여 표현을 다양화

sentences.original: Proponents of mercantilism believed that a nation's wealth was directly proportional to its accumulation of precious metals, particularly gold and silver.
sentences.paraphrase: Those who supported mercantilist principles held the conviction that precious metal accumulation—chiefly gold and silver—determined the extent of a country's economic prosperity.

sentences.original: This ideology prompted governments to implement protectionist policies, including high tariffs and trade restrictions, to maximize exports while minimizing imports.
sentences.paraphrase: Driven by this conviction, government authorities adopted protective trade measures such as steep tariffs and import controls designed to boost outgoing commerce and reduce incoming goods.
sentences.tip: 동사 'implement'를 'adopt'로, 'maximize/minimize'를 'boost/reduce'로 동의어 치환하고 목적 표현을 변경

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to shop online. Others prefer to shop in physical stores. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I prefer shopping in physical stores because I believe it offers several distinct advantages over online shopping.
First, when I shop in person, I can immediately inspect products, touch the materials, and verify quality before making a purchase decision.
For example, when buying clothes at a store, I can try them on to ensure the fit is perfect, unlike online shopping where returns can be inconvenient and time-consuming.
Additionally, in-store shopping allows me to interact with knowledgeable staff members who can provide instant recommendations tailored to my needs.
Therefore, despite the convenience of online platforms, I believe the tangible benefits and personalized service of physical retail make it the superior shopping experience.

listening.title: Student Inquiry About Dormitory Housing Assignment
listening.script:
Student A: Hi, I'm here to ask about my dormitory assignment. I submitted my housing application three weeks ago, but I haven't received a confirmation yet.

Housing Officer: I understand your concern. Let me check our system. May I have your student ID number?

Student A: Sure, it's 2847593.

Housing Officer: Thank you. I see here that your application is still pending review. We typically process assignments within four to six weeks from the submission date. Since you're right at the three-week mark, you should expect a notification by email within the next week or two.

Student A: Okay, that's helpful. One more thing—I requested a double room on the west campus. Is there any way to ensure that preference is considered?

Housing Officer: We certainly take student preferences into account. However, availability depends on demand and remaining capacity. The west campus is quite popular, so I cannot guarantee placement there. But your preference is documented in your file.

Student A: Got it. Thanks so much for your assistance!

Housing Officer: You're welcome. If you don't receive confirmation within two weeks, feel free to visit us again.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Student A's visit?
options: To change his dormitory preference to east campus
To inquire about the status of his housing application
To complain about the slow processing of applications
To request a single room instead of a double room
questions.explanation: 학생 A는 3주 전에 기숙사 신청을 했는데 아직 확인을 받지 못해서 신청 상태를 문의하기 위해 온 것입니다.

questions.q: What does the housing officer suggest about the student's west campus preference?
options: It is guaranteed to be approved
It will definitely be rejected due to high demand
It is recorded in the file, but availability is not certain
He should submit a new preference form immediately
questions.explanation: 주택 담당자는 학생의 선호도가 기록되어 있지만, 웨스트 캠퍼스는 인기가 많아서 배치를 보장할 수 없다고 말합니다.

questions.q: Why does the housing officer mention that the west campus is quite popular?
options: To encourage the student to change his preference
To explain that the student's request may not be fulfilled due to high demand
To suggest that the student should have applied earlier
To indicate that all dormitory assignments are completed
questions.explanation: 담당자는 웨스트 캠퍼스가 인기 있다는 점을 언급함으로써 학생의 선호가 충족되지 않을 수 있음을 설명합니다.
